subject: [Halfway check] OKR status, scope adjustments, and unblock requests
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@acme.com>
Cc: James Lee <james.lee@acme.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Halfway checkpoint: OKR status, scope adjustments, and unblock requests

Team + Sarah —

We're at the halfway point for Q3 and I want to align on a tight set of asks we need to close before the QBR. TL;DR: overall on track but two engineering dependencies and one procurement item are blocking the ACME rollout milestone (OKR-2.1).

Attached: QBR_prep_deck_v1.pdf (draft) and an OKR status sheet — please review before EOD Friday.

Current state (brief):
- OKR-1 (runtime stability): On track (green) — minor latencies under load, dashboards look good.
- OKR-2 (enterprise pilots / ACME): Yellow — we have functional integration but need 2 items below to avoid scope pull.
- OKR-3 (cost/perf optimizations): On track but depends on OKR-2 kernel tuning work.

Concrete asks (what I need by Wednesday 9/16):
1) From ACME (Sarah/James): confirm expected monthly QPS distribution and peak tail latency SLOs so we can finalize the capacity plan (we used conservative numbers in the deck).
2) From Eng (Karthik + Laura): commit a timeline for the KV cache fix (SUP-1234) and a one-week safe rollback plan if the kernel change regresses.
3) Procurement: Marissa, I need approval to expedite the reserved instance add-on for Dedicated for two weeks of burst capacity (cost impact in the attached).

Risk if not resolved: we'll need to ship ACME with the lower-throughput plan (reduce max sessions by 25%) — that would push ARR ramp and influence the QBR narrative.

Next steps:
- Sarah: can you reply with the QPS numbers and whether ACME can accept a staged rollout?
- Karthik/Laura: reply with SUP-1234 ETA and rollback plan.
- Marissa: can finance greenlight the short reserved capacity bump?

Thanks — short call OK if that's easier. I put a 15-min slot on the calendar for Tue 9/15 at 16:00 PT but can move.

—
Mateo Alvarez
Director, Growth Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@acme.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: James Lee <james.lee@acme.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Halfway checkpoint: OKR status, scope adjustments, and unblock requests

Thanks Mateo — quick answers below.

1) QPS & SLOs: our initial ramp is 40k QPS daily average across EU/US with spikes to ~120k QPS during batch windows (we can provide sample traces). For latency, the business needs p95 < 350ms, p99 < 700ms for the critical route. We can tolerate a staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) if you provide a rollback path.

2) Monitoring/evidence: we'll need access to token-level cost estimates and a trimmed set of the dashboard panels for the first two weeks post-launch. Can you provide a temporary read-only link?

3) Procurement: ACME is comfortable covering the short-term extra capacity cost if Redwood can guarantee no data retention beyond session TTL and provide SOC2 evidence for the Dedicated pool.

We can join the Tue 9/15 16:00 PT slot — Sarah and James will be there.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Halfway checkpoint: OKR status, scope adjustments, and unblock requests

Mateo —

We investigated SUP-1234 (KV cache eviction under burst). Summary: root cause is an edge-case mutex between the prefetch path and eviction routine under certain shard patterns. Fix is ~3 dev days + 2 days QA. Plan and mitigations:
- Day 0-3: patch and unit tests (branch: hotfix/sup-1234).
- Day 4-5: canary rollout to lower-priority pool; monitor p95/p99 and KV hit-rate.
- If regressions, we have a fallback to disable the prefetch optimization in runtime flags (instant rollback).

I'll reserve an engineer for the Tue 9/15 16:00 PT call to walk ACME through the rollback plan. Also linking the JIRA: SUP-1234 and a brief runbook.

Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager

Mateo — acknowledged. Quick update and next actions: 

- KV cache hotfix: Karthik's timeline looks good. I've added a short test matrix: spike generator + integration test with the ACME sample traces (will run Tue night).
- Reserved capacity: I spoke with finance; Marissa, please see attached cost delta (QBR_prep_deck_v1.pdf page 6) — we can absorb the two-week burst for the pilot if ACME signs the SOC2 addendum.
- QBR rehearsal: recommend a 20-min dry run Wed 9/23 10:00 PT with Marissa to lead the commercial narrative, Mateo to run the technical deck, and Karthik to cover rollbacks.

Attachments: okrs_halfway_status.xlsx (updated), small runbook snippet (hotfix steps).
